links.outcome: Change in LLM adverse event predictions when persona socio-demographic attributes varied
links.effect: Systematic disparities in AE prediction accuracy; disadvantaged groups (low education, unstable housing) were frequently assigned higher predicted AE likelihoods than privileged groups (postgraduate-educated, privately insured).
links.quote: Disadvantaged groups (e.g., low education, unstable housing) were frequently assigned higher predicted AE likelihoods than more privileged groups (e.g., postgraduate-educated, privately insured).

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating demographic bias and reliability in LLMs for adverse event predictions across simulated user personas and roles.
